newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends down as soybeans fall, soyoil up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends down as soybeans fall, soyoil up.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended lower Thursday, hit by a late sell-off in soybeans, while soyoil closed firmer on continued commercial interest amid talk China was buying Argentine soyoil, traders said.

Argentine traders said exporters were doing bumper trade in soybean oil, with China leading the pack of Asian buyers seeking soyoil. They said Brazil and Argentina were shipping roughly 0.5 million tonnes of sunflower oil and soyoil a month, and China was taking about a third of that.
Both markets had been higher most of the session, boosted by bullishly construed USDA weekly export sales data.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended May 15 totaled 121,700 tonnes, above expectations for 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes.
Soyoil net export sales for the week ended May 15 totaled 5,400 tonnes, above expectations for 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes.
Soymeal ended $2.50 to $0.20 lower, with July off $1.00 at $283.80 a ton. Soyoil settled 0.20 to 0.17 cent higher, with July up 0.18 cent at 23.63 cents a lb.
U.S. Census Bureau crush data released Thursday were also deemed supportive although the report showed stocks figures above average trade expectation, analysts said.

"I think the census data was pretty supportive for soy products, considering the crushings came in one million bushels above expectation and the stocks were still within expectations," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "
Census showed meal stocks at 280,058 tons, above average trade expectation. Soyoil stocks of 2.164 billion lbs were also above average expectation but both figures were within analysts' range.

"From a longer term perspective, the market for meal is trading 13 percent higher than last year, we're crushing more than a year ago and our stocks are less than a year ago," said Bill Biedermann, analyst with Allendale Inc.

On the day, commercials were again buyers of soyoil but on a smaller scale than Wednesday. ADM bought 150 lots August and 50 September. Cargill Inc bought 500 July and 100 each August and September, traders said.
Merrill Lynch sold 500 July and Dean Witter sold 200 July.
Central Soya spread at least 500 July/December at 0.55 cent per lb, premium December.
In soymeal, Continental Grain sold 400 July, Merrill Lynch sold 400 July and Dean Witter bought 300 July while Iowa Grain and Smith Barney each bought 200 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 26,892. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Wednesday's 25,208.
